_readme: EDITABLE BY THE HOSPITAL. This file contains NO medicines or doses on purpose. It lists investigations, monitoring, escalation, source search and prevention only. Treatment decisions belong entirely to the treating clinician and the local sepsis pathway.

hour1_bundle.lactate: Check lactate (blood test); repeat in 2-4 h if raised.
hour1_bundle.cultures: Consider taking blood cultures and cultures from the suspected source (before any treatment is started, if no delay).
hour1_bundle.treatment_review: Prompt the treating physician to review, without delay, whether time-critical sepsis treatment is needed, following the local sepsis pathway. Choice of treatment is the doctor's decision.
hour1_bundle.perfusion_review: Low BP or high lactate: urgent bedside assessment of circulation, hydration status and urine output by a physician.
hour1_bundle.escalation: BP still low after physician review: escalate to ICU / senior doctor.
hour1_bundle.source_control: Identify the likely source and discuss source control (drain, debride, remove infected device) with the senior team.

respiratory.label: Respiratory sepsis (lungs)
workup: Chest X-ray (or CT)
Oxygenation check: SpO2 and blood gas
Sputum / tracheal aspirate culture
Auscultate chest for focal crackles
source_control: Airway clearance and respiratory support as the physician decides
red_flags: Falling SpO2 or rising respiratory rate: urgent senior / ICU review

urosepsis.label: Urosepsis (urinary tract / kidney)
workup: Urinalysis (pus cells, nitrite) and urine culture
Renal ultrasound / CT if obstruction suspected (flank pain, low urine output)
Check for an indwelling urinary catheter
source_control: Remove or replace the urinary catheter
red_flags: Infected and obstructed kidney is a urological emergency

abdominal.label: Abdominal sepsis
workup: Abdominal exam: rigidity, guarding, tenderness
Liver function tests; amylase / lipase if indicated
Ultrasound or CT abdomen; erect chest X-ray for free air
source_control: Urgent surgical / interventional review for perforation, abscess, cholangitis or ischaemic bowel
red_flags: Rigid (board-like) abdomen or free air: surgical emergency
Fever + jaundice + right upper abdominal pain: suspect biliary infection, urgent senior review

bloodstream.label: Bloodstream sepsis (including line-related)
workup: Two sets of blood cultures from separate sites
If a line is present: one culture from the line and one peripheral
Inspect IV / central line sites for redness or pus
Listen for a new murmur; look for nail / skin signs; discuss echocardiography if suspected
source_control: Consider removing the suspected line if other access exists
red_flags: Positive cultures with a new murmur: suspect endocarditis, urgent senior review

skin.label: Skin and soft-tissue sepsis
workup: Mark the border of the redness and re-check hourly
Compare pain level with how the skin looks
Look for blisters, dark / black skin, crepitus
Wound / tissue culture; imaging only if it does not delay surgical review
source_control: Urgent surgical review: debridement is the main source control
red_flags: Pain out of proportion, fast-spreading redness, blisters / black skin or crepitus: suspect necrotising infection - SURGICAL EMERGENCY, call the surgeon immediately

cns.label: CNS (NOT covered by this prototype)
workup: Neurological exam, GCS, imaging then lumbar puncture if safe
Systematic search for source: chest (X-ray), urine, skin and wounds, lines/catheters, abdomen, CNS if altered mental state
Review recent procedures, travel, immunosuppression, prior culture results

reassessment: Re-check vitals, urine output, mental state and capillary refill at least hourly while High risk.
Re-check lactate in 2-4 h if raised; aim for a falling trend.
Review culture results daily and share them with the treating team.
Escalate to ICU / senior review if risk stays High or MAP / lactate worsen.

general: Daily review: is every line and catheter still needed? Remove early.
Hand hygiene before and after every patient contact.
Good glycaemic control and nutrition support.
respiratory: Ventilator bundle: head of bed 30-45 degrees, oral care, daily sedation / weaning review
Encourage deep breathing and coughing; aspiration precautions
urosepsis: Remove the urinary catheter as soon as possible; keep a closed drainage system
abdominal: After surgery: check wound and abdomen daily and report new pain or rigidity early
Aseptic technique for drains; early feeding and mobilisation per surgical team
bloodstream: Aseptic line insertion and maintenance bundle; check dressing daily
Use lines only when needed; label insertion date
skin: Aseptic dressing technique; keep wounds clean and dry; check daily for redness, swelling, discharge
Pressure-area care and early reporting of rapidly spreading redness

prevention_hospital_level: Routine sepsis screening on every ward using an early warning score plus this alert.
Antimicrobial stewardship: culture-guided, shortest effective course.
Vaccination programmes (influenza, pneumococcal and others per national schedule).
Infection-control audits: CLABSI, CAUTI, VAP and surgical-site infection rates.
Staff training on the Hour-1 sepsis bundle and escalation pathways.
disclaimer: Decision SUPPORT only. The system suggests tests, monitoring, escalation and prevention, never medicines or doses. A qualified clinician verifies against the local sepsis protocol and decides every action.
